entries.sanskrit: द्वादशे तु कुमारादि-मनः-सर्गासमेधनात् । काय-द्वैधेन यौनस् तु मनु-सर्गोऽनुवर्ण्यते ॥
word_for_word: because the creation of mind beginning with the Kumāras has not prospered
entries.literal_english: In the twelfth chapter, because the creation of the mind beginning with the Kumāras has not prospered, the creation of Manu through the division of the body is described.

entries.sanskrit: अग्र इति । ब्रह्मा स्व-सृष्टौ प्रथमम् अविद्या-वृत्तीः ससर्ज । तत्र तमो नाम स्वरूपाप्रकाशः । मोहो देहाद्य्-अहं-बुद्धिः । महा-मोहो भोगेच्छा । तामिस्रं तत्-प्रतिघाते क्रोधः । अन्ध-तामिस्रं तन्-नाशेऽहम् एव मृतोऽस्मीति बुद्धिः । तद् एवोक्तं वैष्णवे--- > तमोऽविवेको मोहः स्याद् अन्तः-क्रण-विभ्रमः । > > महा-मोहस् तु विज्ञेयो ग्राम्य-भोग-सुखैषणा ॥ > > मरणं ह्य् अन्ध-तामिस्रं तामिस्रः क्रोध उच्यते । > > अविद्या पञ्च-पर्वैषा प्रादुर्भूता महात्मनः ॥ इति । पातञ्जलेऽप्य् एत एवोक्ताः---अविद्यास्मिता-राग-द्वेषाभिनिवेशाः पञ्च क्लेशाः इति । श्री-विष्णुस्वामि-प्रोक्ता वा, अज्ञान-विपर्यास-भेद-भय-शोकाः । तद् उक्तं स्वादृग्-उत्थ-विपर्यास इत्य्-आदि ॥२॥
word_for_word: the notion ‘I am the body and so forth’
ignorance, egoism, attachment, aversion and clinging
ignorance, misapprehension, difference, fear and grief
entries.literal_english: “At the beginning” means that Brahmā first created the modes of ignorance in his own creation. Darkness is failure to reveal the true nature; delusion is the notion “I am the body and so forth”; great delusion is the desire for enjoyment; tāmisra is anger when enjoyment is obstructed; and andha-tāmisra is the conviction “I alone am dead” when that enjoyment is destroyed. The Vaiṣṇava teaching and Patañjali’s five afflictions express the same fivefold ignorance; Viṣṇusvāmin explains them as ignorance, misapprehension, difference, fear and grief.

entries.sanskrit: यद्यपि प्रतिकल्पं सनकादि-सृष्टिर् नास्ति, तथापि ब्राह्म-सर्गत्वाद् इहोच्यते । वस्तुतस् तु मुख्य-सर्गादय एव प्रतिकल्पं भवन्ति, सनकादयस् तु ब्राह्म-कल्प-सृष्टा एवानुवर्तन्ते ॥४॥
word_for_word: the creation of Sanaka and others is not in every kalpa
because it belongs to Brahmā’s creation
continue as creations of the Brahma-kalpa
entries.literal_english: Although the creation of Sanaka and the others does not occur in every kalpa, it is mentioned here because it belongs to Brahmā’s creation. Properly, the principal creations occur in every kalpa, while Sanaka and the others continue as creations of the Brahma-kalpa.

entries.sanskrit: त्वत् त्वत्तो ये पूर्वे ब्रह्मादयोऽन्ये वा तैर् एतन् न कृतम् । अपरे त्वत्तोऽर्वाचीनास् तेऽपि न करिष्यन्ति । अङ्गजं कामम् ॥३०॥
word_for_word: those who came before, Brahmā and the others
this was not done by them

entries.literal_english: “Tvat” means “from you.” Those before you, Brahmā and others, did not do this; those later than you will not do it either. “Aṅgaja” means desire.

entries.sanskrit: चातुर्-होत्रं होत्रादीनां चतुर्णां कर्म । कर्म-तन्त्रं यज्ञ-विस्तारः । उपवेदैर् न्यायैश् च सह । आश्रमास् तद् वृत्तयश् चासन् ॥३५॥
word_for_word: the work of the four priests
the work of the four beginning with hotṛ
together with ancillary Vedas and logical disciplines
the āśramas and their duties also arose
entries.literal_english: Cātur-hotram is the work of the four priests beginning with the hotṛ. The karma-tantra is the expansion of sacrificial action, together with the ancillary Vedas and logical disciplines. The āśramas and their respective duties also arose.

entries.sanskrit: चातुर्-होत्र-सृष्टि-क्रमम् आह---शस्त्रम् अप्रगीत-मन्त्र-स्तोत्रं होतुः कर्म । इज्याम् अध्वर्योः कर्म । स्तुति-स्तोमं स्तुतिः सङ्ग ईतं, स्तोमं तद् अर्थम् ऋक्सम् उदायं त्रि-वृत् स्तोमो भवति इत्य्-आदि-विहितम् उद्गातृ-प्रयोज्यम् । प्रायश्चित्तं ब्राह्मम् ॥३७॥
entries.literal_english: He now explains the order of the four-priest creation. Śastra is the hotṛ’s recitation of mantras and hymns not set to melody. Ijyā is the adhvaryu’s work. Stuti and stoma are the udgātṛ’s praise and its prescribed melodic arrangement. Prāyaścitta is the brāhma priest’s work.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.

entries.sanskrit: उपवेद-क्रमम् आह---आयुर्वेदाम् इति । आत्मनो मुखैः । स्थापत्यं विश्वकर्म-शास्त्रम् ।
word_for_word: he explains the order of the ancillary Vedas
entries.literal_english: He now explains the order of the ancillary Vedas. Āyurveda arose from the self’s mouths. Sthāpatya is the science of Viśvakarmā.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: कर्म-तन्त्र-क्रमम् आह---षोडश्य्-उक्थाव् इति । पुरीषी चयनम् । अग्निष्टुद् अग्निष्टोमः ॥४०॥
word_for_word: he explains the order of the ritual system
purīṣī is the piling of the altar
entries.literal_english: He now explains the order of the ritual system. Ṣoḍaśī and uktha are the relevant rites; purīṣī is the piling of the fire altar; and agniṣṭud means agniṣṭoma.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: karma-tantra-kramam āha---ṣoḍaśy-ukthāv iti | purīṣī cayanam | agniṣṭud agniṣṭomaḥ ||40||

entries.sanskrit: विद्येति शौचम् । क्षेत्र-ज्ञस्येश्वर-ज्ञानाद् विशुद्धिः परमा मता इति स्मृतेः । दानम् इति दया, भूताभय-प्रदानस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् इति वचनात् । एवं च, तपः शौचं दया सत्यम् इति पादाः कृते कृताः\[भा।पु। १.१७.२४\] इति प्रथम-स्कन्धोक्तेर् अविरोधः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: through knowledge of the Lord, the knower of the field
of giving fearlessness to living beings
entries.literal_english: Vidya means purity. According to the remembered teaching, purity is supreme purification through knowledge of the Lord, the knower of the field. Dāna means compassion, for no gift of fearlessness to living beings is surpassed. Thus there is no contradiction with the First Canto’s statement that austerity, purity, compassion and truth are the four legs of the age of truth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: vidyeti śaucam | kṣetra-jñasyeśvara-jñānād viśuddhiḥ paramā matā iti smṛteḥ | dānam iti dayā, bhūtābhaya-pradānasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm iti vacanāt | evaṃ ca, tapaḥ śaucaṃ dayā satyam iti pādāḥ kṛte kṛtāḥ\[bhā|pu| 1.17.24\] iti prathama-skandhokter avirodhaḥ ||41||

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचर्याद्य्-आश्रमेष्व् एकैकस्य चातुर्-विध्यम् आह---सावित्रं ब्रह्मचर्यं, उपनयनाद् आरभ्य गायत्रीम् अधीयानस्य त्रि-रात्रम् । प्राजापत्यं व्रतान्य् आचरतः संवत्सरम् । ब्राह्मं वेद-ग्रहणान्तम् । बृहन् नैष्ठिकम् । वार्ता अनिषिद्ध-कृष्य्-आदि-वृत्तिः । सञ्चयो याजनादि-वृत्तिः । शालीनम् अयाचित-वृत्तिः । शिलोञ्छः पतित-कणिश-कण-वृत्तिः । एक-वचनम् आर्षम् । इत्य् एता गृहे वृत्तय इति । यद् वा, शिलोञ्छ इति द्वन्द्वैक्ये सप्तमी । एवं वृत्ति-भेदे सति गृहे स्थिता भवन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥४२॥
word_for_word: in the āśramas beginning with brahmacarya
work such as officiating for others
living on what is not begged
entries.literal_english: He describes four forms within each āśrama beginning with brahmacarya. Sāvitra is the three-night period of study beginning with initiation; prājāpatya is observance of vows for a year; brāhma lasts until the Veda is mastered; and bṛhat is lifelong celibacy. The householders’ livelihoods are: vārtā, permitted agriculture and similar work; sañcaya, work such as officiating for others; śālīna, living on what is not begged; and śiloñcha, gathering fallen grains. The forest-dwellers are four: vaikhanasa, living on uncultivated produce; vālakilya, abandoning stored food when fresh food is found; audumbara, living on fruits gathered from the direction first seen at dawn; and phenapa, living on naturally fallen fruit. The renunciants are kuṭīcaka, whose own āśrama duties are primary; bahvoda, for whom knowledge is primary and ritual subsidiary; haṃsa, fixed in the practice of knowledge; and niṣkriya, one who has attained the truth. Each is superior to the preceding one.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: brahmacaryādy-āśrameṣv ekaikasya cātur-vidhyam āha---sāvitraṃ brahmacaryaṃ, upanayanād ārabhya gāyatrīm adhīyānasya tri-rātram | prājāpatyaṃ vratāny ācarataḥ saṃvatsaram | brāhmaṃ veda-grahaṇāntam | bṛhan naiṣṭhikam | vārtā aniṣiddha-kṛṣy-ādi-vṛttiḥ | sañcayo yājanādi-vṛttiḥ | śālīnam ayācita-vṛttiḥ | śiloñchaḥ patita-kaṇiśa-kaṇa-vṛttiḥ | eka-vacanam ārṣam | ity etā gṛhe vṛttaya iti | yad vā, śiloñcha iti dvandvaikye saptamī | evaṃ vṛtti-bhede sati gṛhe sthitā bhavantīty arthaḥ ||42||

entries.sanskrit: वने स्थिताश् चत्वारः । तत्र वैखानसा अकृष्ट-पच्य-वृत्तयः । वालखिल्या नवेऽन्ने लब्धे पूर्व-सञ्चितान्न-त्यागिनः । औदुम्बराः प्रातर् उत्थाय यां दिशं प्रथमं पश्यन्ति तत आहृतैः फलादिभिर् जीवन्तः । फेनपाः स्वयं पतितैः फलादिभिर् जीवन्तः । कुटीचकः स्वाश्रम-कर्म-प्रधानः । बह्वोदः कर्मोपसर्जनी-कृत्य ज्ञान-प्रधानः । हंसो ज्ञानाभ्यास-निष्ठः । निष्क्रियः प्राप्त-तत्त्वः । एते च सर्वे यथोत्तरं श्रेष्ठाः ॥४३॥
entries.literal_english: There are four forest-dwelling orders. Vaikhanasas live on uncultivated produce; vālakilyas abandon stored food when fresh food is obtained; audumbaras live on fruit and other food gathered from the direction first seen after rising in the morning; and phenapas live on naturally fallen fruit. Kuṭīcaka makes the duties of his own āśrama primary; bahvoda makes knowledge primary and ritual subsidiary; haṃsa is fixed in the practice of knowledge; and niṣkriya has attained the truth. Each is successively superior.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: vane sthitāś catvāraḥ | tatra vaikhānasā akṛṣṭa-pacya-vṛttayaḥ | vālakhilyā nave’nne labdhe pūrva-sañcitānna-tyāginaḥ | audumbarāḥ prātar utthāya yāṃ diśaṃ prathamaṃ paśyanti tata āhṛtaiḥ phalādibhir jīvantaḥ | phenapāḥ svayaṃ patitaiḥ phalādibhir jīvantaḥ | kuṭīcakaḥ svāśrama-karma-pradhānaḥ | bahvodaḥ karmopasarjanī-kṛtya jñāna-pradhānaḥ | haṃso jñānābhyāsa-niṣṭhaḥ | niṣkriyaḥ prāpta-tattvaḥ | ete ca sarve yathottaraṃ śreṣṭhāḥ ||43||

entries.sanskrit: न्यायादीनां पूर्वादि-क्रमेणोत्पत्तिम् आह---आन्वीक्षिकीति । आन्वीक्षिक्य्-आद्या मोक्ष-धर्म-कामार्थ-विद्याः । भूर्-भूवः-स्वर् इति व्यस्तास् तिस्रः । समस्ता चतुर्थी । यथाह आश्वलायनः---एवं व्याहृतयः प्रोक्ता व्यस्ताः समस्ताः इति । यद् वा, मह इति चतुर्थी । तथा च श्रुतिः--- > भूर्-भुवः-सुवर् इति वा एतास् तिस्रो व्याहृतयः । तासाम् उ ह स्मैतां > चतुर्थीं माहा-चमस्यः प्रवेदयते मह इति ॥ इति । दह्रतो हृदयाकाशात् ॥४४॥
word_for_word: in the order beginning with logic
the sciences of liberation, dharma, desire and wealth
entries.literal_english: He explains the production of the sciences in the order beginning with logic. Ānvīkṣikī and the other sciences are the disciplines of liberation, dharma, desire and wealth. Bhūr, bhuvar and svar are the three separate vyāhṛtis; together they make the fourth, mahā. The Upaniṣadic teaching likewise presents the three and the fourth great vyāhṛti as arising from the subtle heart-space.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: nyāyādīnāṃ pūrvādi-krameṇotpattim āha---ānvīkṣikīti | ānvīkṣiky-ādyā mokṣa-dharma-kāmārtha-vidyāḥ | bhūr-bhūvaḥ-svar iti vyastās tisraḥ | samastā caturthī | yathāha āśvalāyanaḥ---evaṃ vyāhṛtayaḥ proktā vyastāḥ samastāḥ iti | yad vā, maha iti caturthī | tathā ca śrutiḥ--- > bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvar iti vā etās tisro vyāhṛtayaḥ | tāsām u ha smaitāṃ > caturthīṃ māhā-camasyaḥ pravedayate maha iti || iti | dahrato hṛdayākāśāt ||44||

entries.sanskrit: स्नुतः स्नायुतः । अनुष्टुप् स्नावान् इति श्रुतेः ॥४५॥
entries.literal_english: Snuta means from the sinew; the scripture says, “having sinew.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: snutaḥ snāyutaḥ | anuṣṭup snāvān iti śruteḥ ||45||

entries.sanskrit: महा-कल्पे ब्रह्मा शब्द-ब्रह्म-रूपोऽभवद् इत्य् उक्तं तद् एव दर्शयन् वर्णानाम् उत्पत्तिम् आह---स्पर्श इति सार्धेन । स्पर्शः कादि-वर्ग-पञ्चकम् । स्वरोऽकारादिः । उष्माणः श-ष-स-ह-चतुष्कम् । अन्त-स्था य-र-ल-वाः । सप्त-स्वराः षड्-जादयः। विहारेण क्रीडया ॥४६-४७॥
entries.literal_english: In the great kalpa Brahmā became the form of the Veda’s sound; he now shows that same fact by explaining the origin of the letters. Sparśa means the five consonant groups beginning with ka; svara means the vowels beginning with a; ūṣman means śa, ṣa, sa and ha; antastha means ya, ra, la and va; and the seven notes begin with ṣaḍja. They arose as play.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: mahā-kalpe brahmā śabda-brahma-rūpo’bhavad ity uktaṃ tad eva darśayan varṇānām utpattim āha---sparśa iti sārdhena | sparśaḥ kādi-varga-pañcakam | svaro’kārādiḥ | uṣmāṇaḥ śa-ṣa-sa-ha-catuṣkam | anta-sthā ya-ra-la-vāḥ | sapta-svarāḥ ṣaḍ-jādayaḥ| vihāreṇa krīḍayā ||46-47||

entries.sanskrit: अत एव शब्द-तनुत्वाद् ब्रह्मणः परमेश्वरो नित्यं प्रकाशत इत्य् आह---व्यक्ता वैखरी, अव्यक्तः प्रणवः, तद्-आत्मनस् तस्य ब्रह्मणः परः परमेश्वरोऽवभाति । कीदृशः ? ब्रह्म परिपूर्णः, तत्राव्यक्तात्मनो ब्रह्म-रूपो विततोऽवभटि व्यक्तात्मनो नाना-भक्त्य्-उपबृंहित इन्द्रादि-रूपोऽवभाति ॥४८॥
word_for_word: strengthened by many forms of devotion
entries.literal_english: Because Brahmā has the nature of sound, the Supreme Lord is eternally manifest through him. Vaikharī is the manifest speech and praṇava is unmanifest; beyond that Brahman, the Supreme Lord shines. He is complete Brahman: in the unmanifest aspect He shines as the pervasive Brahman-form, and in the manifest aspect He shines in many forms, strengthened by devotion, beginning with Indra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: ata eva śabda-tanutvād brahmaṇaḥ parameśvaro nityaṃ prakāśata ity āha---vyaktā vaikharī, avyaktaḥ praṇavaḥ, tad-ātmanas tasya brahmaṇaḥ paraḥ parameśvaro’vabhāti | kīdṛśaḥ ? brahma paripūrṇaḥ, tatrāvyaktātmano brahma-rūpo vitato’vabhaṭi vyaktātmano nānā-bhakty-upabṛṃhita indrādi-rūpo’vabhāti ||48||

entries.sanskrit: या पूर्वं विसृष्टा सती नीहारं तमोऽभवत् । ततोऽपराम् अनिषिद्धकाम् आसक्तां तनुम् । शब्द-ब्रह्म-तनुस् तु सदास्त्य् एव । तन्व्-अन्तरग्रहणे कारणम् आह---ऋषीणाम् इत्य्-आदिना ॥४९॥
word_for_word: another body free from prohibited desire and attached to desire
the reason for taking another body
entries.literal_english: The former body, once created, became mist and darkness; thereafter Brahmā assumed another body free from prohibited desire and attached to desire. The body that is sound-Brahman, however, always remains. He now states the reason for taking another body, beginning with “of the sages.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yā pūrvaṃ visṛṣṭā satī nīhāraṃ tamo’bhavat | tato’parām aniṣiddhakām āsaktāṃ tanum | śabda-brahma-tanus tu sadāsty eva | tanv-antaragrahaṇe kāraṇam āha---ṛṣīṇām ity-ādinā ||49||

entries.sanskrit: चिन्ताम् एवाह---अहो इति । व्यपृतस्य व्यापारं कुर्वाणस्य ॥५०॥
entries.literal_english: He describes the thought itself with “alas.” Vyapṛta means one who is engaged in activity.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: cintām evāha---aho iti | vyapṛtasya vyāpāraṃ kurvāṇasya ||50||

entries.sanskrit: युक्त-कृतो यथोचितं कुर्वतः ॥५१॥
entries.literal_english: Of one who acts appropriately, doing what is proper.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yukta-kṛto yathocitaṃ kurvataḥ ||51||

entries.sanskrit: अत एव कस्य ब्रह्मणो रूपं द्विधा भूतम् इत्य् आश्चर्यात् कायम् अद्याप्य् अभिचक्षते ॥५२॥
entries.literal_english: Therefore, because Brahmā’s form became twofold, it is even today called a body, kāya.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: ata eva kasya brahmaṇo rūpaṃ dvidhā bhūtam ity āścaryāt kāyam adyāpy abhicakṣate ||52||

entries.sanskrit: या स्त्री सा अस्य महिष्य् आसीत् ॥५३॥
entries.literal_english: The woman was the great king Manu’s queen.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yā strī sā asya mahiṣy āsīt ||53||

entries.sanskrit: एधां बभूविरे वृद्धिं प्राप्ताः । तद् एवाह---स चापीति ।
entries.literal_english: They increased; they attained growth. He says the same thing with “and he also.”

entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: यतो यासां सन्ततिभिः ॥५६॥
entries.literal_english: By the descendants of whom the world became filled.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
